<reason>B narrowly wins on the proposition as written. Its demand for relevant records and assessment of demonstrated descendant losses supplies a bounded route to stronger repair, which A substantially accepts. A repeatedly shifts the burden toward proving that adequate settlements must remain perpetually open, something the motion does not require. A argues more sharply against speculative inheritance claims and correctly shows that institutional orders can themselves expose private information. Those rebuttals weaken B’s implementation claims, but chiefly justify limits on stronger remedies rather than rejecting them.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s second rebuttal identifies A’s survivor package as conceding stronger redress and specifies assessment of demonstrated descendant losses as an endpoint. A’s subsequent acceptance of such assessment narrows the disagreement without defeating the motion.</best_rebuttal>
